name: Manchester United 1995/96
scopeNote: Manchester United under Alex Ferguson from the opening league match (Aston Villa 1-3, 19 Aug 1995) to the FA Cup final (1-0 Liverpool, 11 May 1996): league and FA Cup double after selling Ince, Hughes and Kanchelskis and promoting Butt, Scholes, Beckham and the Nevilles. Sources describe a conventional 4-4-2 (Tyler: 'the 4-4-2 was reinstated'), with Cantona (back 1 Oct 1995) as the focal player, Keane and Butt in central midfield, Giggs, Beckham and Sharpe wide and Cole/Scholes/McClair up front; no tier A-B source gives a pressing or marking system for this season and no source states zonal or man-to-man, so style is described mainly through lineups, contemporary press (counter-attack, Mail & Guardian) and match accounts. Correction to the brief: Keane arrived in 1993 and was in the 1995/96 side (he played in the opening match and the FA Cup final). Cantona joined in Nov 1992, so he was in United's squad before, but was banned until 1 Oct 1995. The 1996/97 Newcastle 5-0 (Oct 1996) and Beckham's halfway-line goal (Aug 1996) are outside the period and not used. Sources that mention only Ferguson's 1990s teams in general (sigames, fmscout, rosetta/tifo) were not used.
openQuestions: Centre-back pairing at Newcastle on 4 March 1996: Yahoo/Independent says Pallister was injured and Gary Neville played at centre-half; another unverified line-up lists Bruce and May. Not resolved.

No explicit source found on zonal vs man-marking at set pieces for 1995/96; the only evidence is man-oriented marking of the Liverpool playmakers in the FA Cup final as described by Wikipedia - treat as unresolved.

Wikipedia/Sportskeeda say 'Cantona and McManaman marked and closed out by Redknapp and Barnes and Keane and Butt respectively': ambiguous who marked whom; read as each side's playmaker marked by two midfielders.
Did Ferguson play a back three only at Sunderland (6 Jan 1996) or elsewhere? Tyler says he considered it before the final and changed his mind (retrospective, from an 'impeccable source').
Ferguson's mind games (Leeds, 17 Apr 1996) are credited by the press, but Keegan says they did not cause the collapse and Ferguson (per later accounts) aimed them at Wilkinson; contested credit.
